problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate budget across 14 infrastructure projects to maximize the overall community benefit score.  
The characteristics of each project are as follows:  
* Project A: benefit score 0.196, impact index 0.152, allocation limits [0.094, 0.487]  
* Project B: benefit score 0.112, impact index 0.226, allocation limits [0.095, 0.663]  
* Project C: benefit score 0.148, impact index 0.015, allocation limits [0.023, 0.570]  
* Project D: benefit score 0.183, impact index 0.208, allocation limits [0.034, 0.379]  
* Project E: benefit score 0.107, impact index 0.113, allocation limits [0.039, 0.691]  
* Project F: benefit score 0.127, impact index 0.098, allocation limits [0.014, 0.649]  
* Project G: benefit score 0.036, impact index 0.299, allocation limits [0.073, 0.710]  
* Project H: benefit score 0.056, impact index 0.294, allocation limits [0.052, 0.421]  
* Project I: benefit score 0.194, impact index 0.090, allocation limits [0.068, 0.383]  
* Project J: benefit score 0.121, impact index 0.028, allocation limits [0.087, 0.713]  
* Project K: benefit score 0.148, impact index 0.085, allocation limits [0.069, 0.839]  
* Project L: benefit score 0.027, impact index 0.122, allocation limits [0.042, 0.846]  
* Project M: benefit score 0.186, impact index 0.300, allocation limits [0.057, 0.558]  
* Project N: benefit score 0.075, impact index 0.297, allocation limits [0.043, 0.845]  

Each project must receive a budget share within its specified allocation limits, and the total allocation across all projects must sum to one.  
To ensure timely completion, the group of quick-delivery projects Q = {C, E, H, K, L} must collectively receive at least 0.260 of the total budget.  
Additionally, the overall impact index for the portfolio must not exceed 0.192, and the total benefit score must be at least 0.080.  
Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total benefit score while satisfying all constraints.
